description: M8 Google Calendar write integration (tasks.md T8.1-T8.3, FR-39/FR-40). Add a real GoogleCalendarWriter behind the EXISTING CalendarProvider Protocol, disabled by default, explicit-single-event-only (never auto-add), idempotent via a deterministic iCalUID derived from Event.identity_key. Add an 'Add to Calendar' POST route keyed by identity_key with a graceful 'not configured' state when the Null provider is active. All tests use a MOCKED Google client; the google libraries are imported lazily so offline imports never require them. DEPENDS ON nothing in FEAT-001/002 functionally; ordered after them so it stacks cleanly on the same worktree. Independent of FEAT-004.
steps: Run `uv add google-api-python-client google-auth` (updates pyproject.toml + uv.lock).

In vandy_food_radar/config.py add `@dataclass CalendarWriteConfig` with `enabled: bool = False`, `calendar_id: str = ""`, `credentials_json: str = ""`; add `calendar_write: CalendarWriteConfig = field(default_factory=CalendarWriteConfig)` to Config. In Config.from_env read VFR_CALENDAR_WRITE_ENABLED (via _parse_bool), VFR_CALENDAR_ID (reuse or add), and GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CREDENTIALS_JSON into those fields when present. Default provider selection stays CalendarProviderKind.NONE.

In vandy_food_radar/providers/calendar.py add `GoogleCalendarWriter` implementing `add_event(self, event: Event) -> CalendarWriteResult`. Constructor takes an injected `service` (the Google Calendar API client) and `calendar_id: str`, plus a `timezone: str`. Build the event body: summary=event.title; start/end as {dateTime, timeZone} from event.event_date + start_time/end_time using zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(timezone) (when start_time is None, fall back to an all-day {date} entry); location=event.location; description composed from food_description + the event/source URL; and a deterministic `iCalUID` = f"vfr-{event.identity_key}" (stable so a repeat add updates rather than duplicates, FR-40). Call service.events().import_(...) or insert(...) — use import_ with iCalUID for idempotency — inside try/except, returning CalendarWriteResult(ok=True, event_ref=<returned id>) on success and CalendarWriteResult(ok=False, detail=str(err)) on any error (never raises).

In vandy_food_radar/providers/calendar.py add a lazy builder that constructs the real Google service ONLY when needed: import google.oauth2.service_account and googleapiclient.discovery INSIDE the function body (with `# type: ignore[import-untyped]` as needed for mypy strict) so module import stays offline-clean. Extend build_calendar_provider(config): return GoogleCalendarWriter(service=<built from config.calendar_write.credentials_json>, calendar_id=config.calendar_write.calendar_id, timezone=config.timezone) only when config.providers.calendar is CalendarProviderKind.GOOGLE AND config.calendar_write.enabled AND credentials_json present; otherwise return NullCalendarProvider(). Update vandy_food_radar/providers/__init__.py exports to include GoogleCalendarWriter.

In vandy_food_radar/web/app.py add a `calendar_provider: CalendarProvider | None = None` parameter to create_app, defaulting to build_calendar_provider(config) when None. Add route `@app.post('/calendar/add/<identity_key>')` that finds the one event for today's target window matching identity_key (iterate repository.get_events_for_day(window.target_date) and match event.identity_key), skips cancelled events, calls calendar_provider.add_event(event), and redirects to index carrying a status message (use flask flash with a secret_key set on the app, or a query param the index reads) — when the provider is NullCalendarProvider the message is the graceful 'Calendar not configured' text from CalendarWriteResult.detail. Never auto-add on GET or on index render.

In vandy_food_radar/web/templates/_event_card.html add an 'Add to Calendar' button (a small POST form to /calendar/add/{{ card.event.identity_key }}) shown only for non-cancelled events. In vandy_food_radar/web/templates/index.html render any flashed/queried calendar status message near the top. In vandy_food_radar/web/static/app.css add button styling. Wire the Flask app secret_key (from config or a fixed dev value) in create_app if using flash.

Add tests/test_calendar_provider.py: inject a FAKE Google service (a stub whose events().import_(...).execute() records the body and returns {'id': 'evt-1'}) into GoogleCalendarWriter; assert the body maps title/start/end (with timeZone)/location/description correctly, that iCalUID == 'vfr-' + event.identity_key, and that two add_event calls for the same event send the SAME iCalUID (idempotent-by-uid). Assert build_calendar_provider returns NullCalendarProvider when disabled/no creds and (with a monkeypatched lazy builder) a GoogleCalendarWriter when GOOGLE+enabled+creds.

Add to tests/test_web.py a calendar-route test: with the default (Null) provider, POST /calendar/add/<identity_key> for a seeded event redirects (302) and the index then shows the 'not configured' message; with a fake provider injected via create_app(..., calendar_provider=fake), the route calls add_event exactly once for the matching event.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run pytest tests/test_calendar_provider.py tests/test_web.py -q` passes with a MOCKED Google client; no test imports or requires the real google libraries at collection time (lazy import).

GoogleCalendarWriter builds a correct event body and a deterministic iCalUID = 'vfr-'+identity_key; a repeat add uses the same UID (idempotent, FR-40); add_event never raises (errors -> CalendarWriteResult(ok=False,...)).
build_calendar_provider returns GoogleCalendarWriter only when providers.calendar is GOOGLE AND enabled AND creds present; otherwise NullCalendarProvider (default).
POST /calendar/add/<identity_key> adds only the one explicitly selected non-cancelled event (never auto-adds); with the Null provider it surfaces a graceful 'Calendar not configured' state.
`make check` is green; the pre-existing 93 tests still pass.
findings: Implemented M8 Google Calendar write. Added google-api-python-client + google-auth via `uv add` (now in pyproject.toml and the regenerated committed requirements.txt; uv.lock stays gitignored). Added CalendarWriteConfig(enabled=False, calendar_id, credentials_json) to Config with from_env reading VFR_CALENDAR_WRITE_ENABLED, VFR_CALENDAR_ID, and the plain GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CREDENTIALS_JSON; default provider selection stays CalendarProviderKind.NONE. GoogleCalendarWriter sits behind the existing CalendarProvider Protocol: constructor takes an injected service + calendar_id + timezone; add_event builds a body (summary, {dateTime,timeZone} start/end via zoneinfo, all-day {date} fallback when start_time is None, location, description from food_description + event/rsvp URL) with deterministic iCalUID='vfr-'+identity_key and calls service.events().import_(...).execute() inside try/except so it never raises (errors -> CalendarWriteResult(ok=False, detail=str(err))). build_calendar_provider returns GoogleCalendarWriter only when providers.calendar is GOOGLE AND calendar_write.enabled AND credentials_json present, else NullCalendarProvider; the google libs are imported LAZILY inside _build_google_service (narrow `# type: ignore[import-untyped]` on googleapiclient and `# type: ignore[no-untyped-call]` on the credentials call for mypy strict). Web: create_app gains calendar_provider param defaulting to build_calendar_provider(config), a dev secret_key backs flash(), and POST /calendar/add/<identity_key> finds the single matching event for the target window, skips cancelled (VerificationState.CANCELLED), calls add_event, and redirects to index with a flashed status; NullCalendarProvider yields the graceful 'Calendar not configured' text. Templates: 'Add to Calendar' POST form on non-cancelled cards; flashed messages rendered near the top of index.html; button + flash CSS added. Tests: tests/test_calendar_provider.py uses a fake service (events().import_(...).execute() records body, returns {'id':...}) asserting body mapping, iCalUID, idempotent-by-UID, error path, all-day fallback, and build selection (Null when disabled/no creds; GoogleCalendarWriter when GOOGLE+enabled+creds via monkeypatched lazy builder); tests/test_web.py adds Null-provider 'not configured' redirect, fake-provider single add for the matching event, and cancelled-skip. Verification: `uv run pytest tests/test_calendar_provider.py tests/test_web.py -q` passes (15), `uv run mypy` clean (61 files), `make check` green with 133 tests total; confirmed no google libs are imported at module import or test collection time. Note: the FEAT-003 verification set does not include the api/index serverless-boot check (api/index.py + vercel.json belong to FEAT-001/002 and are not present yet); regenerated requirements.txt as the committed manifest since the new deps are runtime deps.
